scope: Canonical AI, tech, and software terms explicitly discussed across the conference transcripts (UNLOCK 2026 and the AI-engineering episodes): AI and machine learning vocabulary, named models and benchmarks (including biological/genomic foundation models, which are model artifacts), and the computing-leaning entries from scientific data and computing. Split on 2026-08-27 from the combined glossary.json (schemaVersion 1, 271 terms) into this file and glossary.biotech.json; term entries are unchanged. Company and person names remain in the conference graph (graph/ai-tech/). Biology, drug-discovery, clinical, and laboratory terms live in glossary.biotech.json.

terms.definition: A strategy in which a model selects the most informative next examples or experiments from which to learn.
An AI system that can plan, use tools, take actions, and iterate toward a goal rather than only produce a single response.
AI designed to carry out multi-step work with some autonomy, often using tools, memory, and feedback.
The structures, policies, review processes, and accountability used to guide how AI is selected, developed, and deployed.
An agentic system intended to perform substantial parts of scientific research, such as literature review, analysis, hypothesis generation, and experiment planning.
A combined abbreviation for artificial intelligence and machine learning.
Frontier AI lab behind the Claude model family (Opus, Sonnet, Fable), Claude Code, and the Claude Cowork enterprise agent.
An application programming interface through which software systems or agents exchange requests and data.
A model that generates an output sequentially, conditioning each new element on previously generated elements.
A standardized collection of tasks, data, and metrics used to compare model capabilities.
A broadly trained model of biological data that can be adapted or prompted for many downstream scientific tasks.
A benchmark for evaluating whether agents can explore biological datasets, perform multi-step analyses, and interpret the results.
A model intended to represent or predict the effects of interventions and counterfactual changes.
Prediction of how a biological system will change after a specified genetic, chemical, or environmental intervention.
A method that represents single-cell gene-expression profiles as ordered gene sequences so language-model techniques can be applied to cellular data.
Anthropic frontier model (Aug 2026).
Anthropic's top frontier model (Aug 2026).
Anthropic's workhorse model family; the customary open-source benchmark comparison point.
An AI agent specialized in writing, running, debugging, and modifying software.
A forecast produced by a mathematical or machine-learning model rather than a direct experiment.
The amount of input and prior output a model can consider in one inference run.
A neural-network architecture that learns local spatial patterns and is widely used for image analysis.
An attention mechanism that lets one representation selectively use information from another representation or modality.
The controlled exchange of datasets between teams or organizations for analysis, model training, validation, or collaboration.
A setting in which too few relevant observations are available to train or validate a model reliably.
A setting with enough relevant observations to train and evaluate models at substantial scale.
Machine learning based on neural networks with multiple learned layers of representation.
Open-weights lab whose v4 generation made open models viable for production agent traffic in 2026.
DeepSeek's open-weights generation adopted for production agent traffic in 2026 (e.g. Lindy's switch from Anthropic).
A generative model that learns to reconstruct structured sequences from noise through iterative denoising rather than only predicting the next token.
A model trained or adapted for the data, vocabulary, and tasks of a particular field.
A learned numeric representation that places data with related properties near one another in a vector space.
A model component that converts raw input into a learned internal representation.
The systematic measurement of whether a model or system performs a defined task reliably and usefully.
Arc Institute's genomic foundation-model family for reading, writing, and reasoning over biological sequences.
The ability to provide human-understandable reasons or evidence for a model's output.
Additional training that adapts a pre-trained model to a narrower dataset or task.
A model trained broadly at scale so it can support many downstream tasks.
A model near the leading edge of capability or scale at a given time.
Google DeepMind's fast, low-cost frontier-tier model (Aug 2026).
A model's ability to perform well on data, contexts, or tasks not seen during training.
A model that learns a data distribution well enough to create or reconstruct new examples.
A foundation model trained on large collections of DNA or other genomic sequences.
Google's frontier AI lab; Gemini model family (Gemini 3.6 Flash current as of Aug 2026).
A family of generative pre-trained transformer models for language and multimodal tasks.
OpenAI's current frontier generation (Aug 2026).
A graphics processing unit, widely used to accelerate neural-network training and inference.
xAI's current frontier model (Aug 2026).
A provider that operates cloud-computing infrastructure at very large scale.
A model's ability to adapt its behavior from examples or information supplied in the current input without updating model weights.
The use of a trained model to generate a prediction, representation, or output.
The degree to which people can inspect or understand a model's internal representations and decision process.
An interactive document that combines executable code, results, visualizations, and explanatory text.
Moonshot AI's current frontier model (Aug 2026); a coding-agent favorite alongside Claude Code and Codex.
Edison Scientific's AI scientist, which combines literature, analysis, and other specialized agents for autonomous scientific discovery.
A benchmark suite for evaluating language models and agents on practical biology-research tasks.
A model trained to represent or generate sequences such as human language, code, proteins, or genes.
A language model trained at large scale on broad data and capable of many language and reasoning tasks.
An internal learned encoding that captures important hidden structure in data.
Lilly's program for making selected AI/ML models available to biotech users in exchange for model-improving data contributions.
Meta's open-weight model family.
A task requiring many dependent actions over an extended period before a useful result is reached.
Methods that learn patterns from data to make predictions, generate outputs, or guide decisions.
A model trained to reconstruct portions of an input that have been hidden or masked.
A self-supervised training task in which a model predicts input tokens that were intentionally hidden.
A server implementing the Model Context Protocol so an AI system can discover and use external tools or data.
Analysis that tries to identify the internal components and computations responsible for a model's behavior.
Open-weight Llama model family; pursuing 'personal superintelligence' and newly open-sourcing frontier models.
Europe's open-weights champion frontier lab.
The structural design of a model, including its components and how information flows between them.
The process of measuring and comparing models on defined datasets, tasks, and metrics.
A partnership in which organizations jointly build, adapt, evaluate, or deploy an AI model.
A learned numeric value that helps determine a model's behavior.
Frontier lab behind the Kimi model family (Kimi K3 current as of Aug 2026).
Data combining distinct measurement types, such as images, gene expression, proteins, clinical records, and text.
A model that learns from or produces more than one type of data.
A machine-learning model composed of connected layers that learn transformations from data.
A training objective in which a model predicts the next element in a sequence from the preceding context.
Noetik's Oncology Counterfactual Therapeutics Oracle, a multimodal world model for simulating patient-level cancer biology.
Noetik's virtual-cell foundation model for simulating spatially resolved single-cell gene expression in tissue.
Frontier AI lab behind the GPT model family (GPT-5.6/Sol generation), the Codex coding agent, and ChatGPT.
Performance in data or biological contexts that differ materially from those used for training.
A framework for retrieving and synthesizing evidence from scientific papers.
AI that perceives, controls, or coordinates actions in the physical world, including robotics and laboratory systems.
Coding-focused foundation model lab; among the American open-models hopefuls.
Initial large-scale training that gives a model broad capabilities before task-specific adaptation.
The use of quantitative models to forecast biological behavior, intervention effects, or patient outcomes.
A sequence model trained on amino-acid strings to learn protein structure, function, or design patterns.
Alibaba's open-weight model family.
A model optimized to perform multi-step inference before producing an answer or action.
Learning internal features from data instead of relying only on manually designed descriptors.
An empirical relationship describing how model performance changes with data, compute, parameters, or another scale variable.
A generative pre-trained transformer for single-cell data that represents genes and expression measurements as model inputs.
An evaluation designed to measure whether an AI system produces correct, reproducible, and useful scientific work.
Training that creates learning targets from the structure of unlabeled data itself.
OpenAI model name in the GPT-5.6 generation (Aug 2026); owner-resolved from ASR 'soul' in the Agent Night panel.
Arc Institute's single-cell foundation model for in-context learning from observational cellular conditions without condition-specific fine-tuning.
Arc Institute's virtual-cell model for predicting cellular responses to perturbations across varied biological contexts.
A self-supervised objective that masks coordinated portions of multiple data modalities so a model must learn cross-modal structure.
US frontier lab; among the American open-models hopefuls.
A discrete unit represented and processed by a sequence model, such as a word fragment, gene, or image patch.
Examples used to estimate a model's parameters or behavior.
A neural-network architecture based on attention mechanisms for modeling relationships within sequences or sets.
The degree of doubt around a prediction or conclusion due to limited data, noise, model assumptions, or unfamiliar context.
A computational model that predicts cellular state or behavior under different biological conditions and perturbations.
A model that learns enough structure and dynamics of a system to simulate possible states, actions, or outcomes.
Xaira's large genome-wide perturbation dataset used to train and evaluate X-Cell.
Xaira Therapeutics' virtual-cell model for predicting causal perturbation effects across diverse cellular contexts.
Frontier lab behind the Grok model family (Grok 4.6 current as of Aug 2026), pursuing a multi-agent product philosophy.
Performance on a task, target, or context without task-specific labeled examples or additional training.
